eval.title: Dollar General Stock Looks More Like An Opportunity, but is Always Retail

call.headline_quote: not for me I'm not going to follow

base_metric.name: net_income
base_metric.quote: everything was great it doubled net income till the end of fiscal 2023 in February but now net income is down and we are around 2 billion

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: if they keep stable 2 billion times 10 20 billion valuation

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: if they continue to grow to 3 billion B ratio 15 20 40 billion valuation that's 50 up

reasons.claim: Without a discount to a conservative valuation the stock offers no margin of safety at the current price.
reasons.quote: there is no margin of safety here

reasons.claim: Retail is a brutally competitive, moat-less business where even successful chains eventually falter, as Buffett himself avoids the sector.
reasons.quote: retail is a Widowmaker because it's a very very hard business to be in

reasons.claim: The multi-year growth trend has stopped, with same-store sales turning negative and sales growth below inflation, justifying the valuation compression from a growth multiple to a value multiple.
reasons.quote: same store sales decreased one percent so that is a negative trend from the growth

data_check.gap_note: he says 0.039, as-of 0.105914 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: same store sales

reasons.claim: A recession would hurt all retailers including dollar stores because falling purchasing power reduces spending across the board, contrary to the common belief that discount retailers benefit in downturns.
reasons.quote: simply everything goes down when there is a recession because of purchasing power going down

reasons.claim: The company keeps investing heavily in new stores rather than returning cash via buybacks, a large ongoing capital commitment relative to market cap even as margins compress.
reasons.quote: no share repurchases so they are focusing on that opening new stores investing into the business a little bit less but still 2 billion of capital Investments

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: capital investments

external_facts_used: Wall Street analyst consensus EPS estimate of 7.75 for this year, down 25%
Analyst projections that earnings will almost triple over the coming seven to eight years, though based on a dwindling number of covering analysts
Warren Buffett's general avoidance of retail stocks
Possibility of an activist investor taking a stake if the market cap fell toward $20 billion

critic.notes: ok — he says no margin of safety, not a value investment, only interesting near $20B with an activist, 'not for me'; the 'small position' aside is speculative, not his recommendation.
